# usrsctp / fuzzer_connect

usrsctp's own fuzz target `fuzzer_connect` ([source](source/fuzzer_connect.c), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over usrsctp (sctplab/usrsctp at fd070e05).

Client socket, connect, optionally injects canned INIT-ACK / COOKIE-ACK / DATA per data[0] bits, then injects data[1..] as one SCTP packet behind a canned common header; nothing about the processing of that packet is checked.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against usrsctp at commit fd070e05 with 1 patch to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source differs from the upstream file at the pinned commit; the copy in source/ is the file as built.

## What the harness checks
- Every socket-setup call (usrsctp_socket, 12 setsockopt, bind, connect == 0 or EINPROGRESS, SCTP_RESET_STREAMS after the canned handshake) must succeed. All run BEFORE the fuzzed packet is injected and depend on the input only through the 8 flag bits of data[0], so this is a finite setup sanity check, not a property of the fuzzed packet ([lines 279-405](source/fuzzer_connect.c#L279-L405)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch usrsctp` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzzer_connect.plain` | 448,384 | `84ea70c612662f19341acf4432396aa4f28d4a597059ca1110e0b9816a141fcc` |
| ubsan | `fuzzer_connect.ubsan` | 505,560 | `a1510803c256b2b60f5eab12007c113a94097cf94d404100baa25723be4c60b1` |
| asan | `fuzzer_connect.asan` | 1,775,864 | `3034af64aadd78c1bd13c4d3dc3f079f351769db199df2c938d108df9e44fcdb` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzzer_connect.asan-ubsan` | 1,840,568 | `9423e008b0b7681001a8dac49cafa42414bbd546db5a8072a9c7520564b1f0af` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
